Kaiyue Zhao


harshitha.rv


Tue, 11/03/2026 - 11:02


**Where are you located? What geographical region(s) do you cover?**
I am based in Beijing, China, supporting research sites in Beijing, Shenyang, Harbin, Chifeng, Weifang and Haikou. Depending on project needs, I also collaborate with sites and study teams across other regions of China. Working with sites throughout the country allows me to experience different research environments, build strong relationships with site teams and develop a broader perspective on clinical research in China.


**How long have you been working in the area of clinical research?**
I have worked in clinical research since graduating from university in 2018. I joined Fortrea, formerly Covance, as a Study Start-Up specialist in December 2018 before transitioning into a Clinical Research Associate role in 2020. Since then, I have gained experience across different functions and contributed to a variety of clinical studies. It is rewarding to see innovative therapies progress through development and know that my work may help bring new treatment options to patients.


**What is the best part of your job?**
The best part of my role is contributing to the development of new medicines that may improve patients’ lives. Although I am not directly involved in treating patients or conducting laboratory research, I play an important role in supporting the quality, integrity and compliance of clinical studies. Every detail matters when turning scientific ideas into potential therapies. I also value the opportunity to learn continuously and collaborate with investigators, study coordinators, sponsors and colleagues across different teams.


**What has been interesting about your work in clinical research? Did anything surprise you about the patient population?**
One of my most memorable experiences took place during a Pre-Study Visit with a Principal Investigator who was also the president of a major hospital. During the visit, I saw first-hand how he balanced patient care, clinical research, hospital operations and public responsibilities while remaining fully engaged in the study. A patient attending the clinic that day was also a surgeon who had travelled from another city for his advice. Watching their interaction reminded me that clinical research is about more than protocols and data. It is about people, their dedication and their shared commitment to advancing medicine.


**What are you most proud of in your work?**
I am proud of the work I do supporting sites and study teams in delivering high-quality clinical research while keeping patient safety and data integrity at the centre of everything we do. Clinical research is a team effort, and my role gives me the opportunity to connect different stakeholders, help solve challenges and support sites throughout the study lifecycle.


Senior Clinical Research Associate
